Kill switch, step 3 of the desktop plan - the Linux block: LinuxVpnKillSwitch, an nftables table of ours (inet vpnhood_kill_switch) that every change replaces whole in one `nft -f`, with no gap. Its output chain lets through the tunnel's interface, loopback, the service (its cgroup), DHCP and NDP, an out-of-tunnel plan's resolvers, then blocks DNS - a LAN router's too - then lets the device-level split through and blocks the rest; its forward chain lets forwarded traffic into and out of the tunnel and to the split only. A blocked TCP connect is reset, as one only dropped times out and leaves an app hanging; UDP is dropped, which fails a send at once. A copy without the service's cgroup rule, as a cgroup's path is gone after a reboot, is loaded at boot by a systemd unit before network-pre.target, so a crash of the service and a reboot keep the block. The table's comment names the app whose block it is by a hash of its owner. On both platforms the owner is the app's storage folder, which an update keeps, where the exe's version folder changes, so a person's disconnect after an update still lifts its own block. The Linux installer installs nftables where it is missing (Debian 13's cloud image) Tested: on the Ubuntu 26.04 and Debian 13 VMs against the server VM - connected, the tunnel and the LAN split pass and DNS to the LAN router is blocked; the service killed, after its restart and after an error stop, a TCP connect is refused at once, DNS fails (EPERM) and the LAN split passes; a reboot while blocked keeps it from boot, with the unit active before network-pre.target, and a connect from it works; a person's disconnect lifts it and removes its boot copy; the switch off and on during a session lifts it and puts it back with the session kept. The owner change rechecked on the Windows Server 2025 Desktop VM. VpnHood.Test and VpnHood.AppLib.Test on a clean HEAD with these files (but VpnTunnelLockTest's three OS-lock tests, which another app's tunnel lock fails here, and a WebSocket padding test once under the suite's load, which passes alone).
